newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Playing moves in Iomega, Robotics.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Playing moves in Iomega, Robotics.

text.p: Volatile moves in two high-tech stocks, Iomega Corp and U.S. Robotics, drove options volumes sharply higher, traders said Tuesday.
Both Iomega and U.S. Robotics options trade on the Chicago Board Options Exchange and American Stock Exchange, but Iomega also trades on the Philadelphia and Pacific stock exchanges.
As on Monday, the Iomega December 25 calls drew most interest as the stock traded around that strike price.
A total of about 13,900 Iomega December 25 calls traded by 1345 CST (2045 GMT).
"There was a big move (in the stock) this morning, so people were looking for the at-the-moneys," one trader on the floor of the CBOE said.
Iomega shares, which rallied 2-5/8 on Monday, climbed another point in early trading Tuesday, reaching a session high of 26-1/4.
With an hour of trading left, the stock was down 5/8 at 24-5/8 on consolidated volume of 6.8 million shares.
"It's been both ways, buyers and sellers," the trader said of Iomega options activity. "I think people bought in the morning when it ran up and now they're getting back out."
Traders said the stock appeared to be caught up in a sector rally, with nothing specific to Iomega driving it up.
Front-month volatility in the Iomega options rose to the mid-60s from around 60, the trader at the CBOE said.
Still, volatilities were 20 to 25 points lower across the board than when the stock was traded on the Nasdaq market. The stock moved to the New York Stock Exchange on November 8.
The trader noted that volatilities in the December series were lower than in later months, possibly because of the holidays late in December. Typically volatility drops off after the front month.
Heavy put and call buying was seen in U.S. Robotics options, with call activity marked by one buyer of 4,000 December 85 calls, traders said.
U.S. Robotics shares were down 5-1/2 at 75-3/8 at 1420 CST (2020 GMT) on heavy volume of more than 9.1 million shares.
Traders said an analyst at Needham & Co warned that U.S. Robotics' current fiscal first quarter may be weak as the company makes the transition to new technology.
Needham declined comment.
Among U.S. Robotics options, the December 85 call was most active, with a total of 4,850 contracts changing hands.
The December 80 call traded about 3,660 contracts.
"There have been a lot of 50-lot and 100-lot put buyers," a trader at the CBOE said.
The busiest put was the December 75, which traded a total of 3,165 contracts. The December 70 put traded 2,450.
Tuesday's drop snapped a four-session rally in U.S. Robotics shares that took them to 81 from around 70.
